title: Respond Without Translating
weekly_can_do: I can respond to familiar professional questions clearly and promptly without mentally constructing every sentence first.

curriculum_constraints.claim_policy: Reported needs remain reported until verified by performance evidence.

traceability.observable_behavior: Produces a connected professional response with reduced preparation delay and uses repair/paraphrase instead of abandoning the message.

sessions.title: Answer Before You Translate
sessions.can_do: I can answer routine professional questions using short response frames without first translating a full answer.
sessions.foundation: Use accessible response frames: From my experience..., The main issue is..., At the moment..., What we need to do is...
sessions.b2_lift: Extend a response with reason, example, qualification and consequence.
sessions.b2_performance: Respond to six realistic colleague questions with decreasing preparation time.
sessions.pronunciation_focus: thought groups and pausing at meaning boundaries
sessions.mediation_move: relay a short field update to a colleague in simpler language
chunks: what we need to do is
interaction_expressions: Let me give you an example.
sessions.evidence: Record response latency, completion, repair strategy and teacher observations; do not infer CEFR from this task alone.

sessions.title: Keep the Message Moving
sessions.can_do: I can continue speaking when I cannot immediately remember a word.
sessions.foundation: Use simple paraphrase frames: It's a person who..., It's something we use for..., What I mean is...
sessions.b2_lift: Circumlocute precisely, reformulate and self-repair without losing the conversational turn.
sessions.b2_performance: Explain professional concepts while selected target words are unavailable.
sessions.pronunciation_focus: chunking and stress on key content words
sessions.mediation_move: explain an unfamiliar project term to a non-specialist colleague
chunks: another way to say it is
interaction_expressions: I can't remember the exact word, but...
What I'm trying to say is...
sessions.evidence: Track whether communication continues successfully when lexical retrieval fails.

sessions.title: Professional Conversation
sessions.can_do: I can sustain a short professional conversation and respond to follow-up questions.
sessions.b2_lift: Qualify claims, react to another speaker and extend the exchange independently.
sessions.b2_performance: Participate in a simulated coordination conversation about a field activity.
sessions.mediation_move: summarise one colleague's concern before giving a response
sessions.evidence: Capture response continuity, interaction management and use of repair strategies.

sessions.title: Unexpected Questions
sessions.can_do: I can respond to an unexpected professional question without freezing or abandoning my message.
sessions.foundation: Use thinking-time phrases without excessive fillers.
sessions.b2_lift: Respond with stance, qualification, evidence and uncertainty where appropriate.
sessions.b2_performance: Handle unpredictable follow-up questions during a short project briefing.
sessions.pronunciation_focus: contrastive stress for key decisions and priorities
sessions.mediation_move: respond to a manager's question by synthesising two pieces of information
interaction_expressions: Let me think for a moment.
Based on the information we have...
There are two things to consider.
sessions.evidence: Compare first and second attempts; improvement is evidence, not proof of a permanent learner trait.

sessions.title: Unseen Transfer Check
sessions.can_do: I can use this week's communication strategies in a new professional situation with minimal support.
sessions.foundation: No pre-teaching of the transfer scenario.
sessions.b2_lift: Independently organise, extend, clarify and repair responses.
sessions.b2_performance: Complete a new 5-7 minute professional conversation containing routine and unexpected questions.
sessions.mediation_move: briefly relay a third party's information before responding

decision_rule.PASS: Target behavior transfers to the unseen scenario with adequate independence.
decision_rule.PARTIAL: Target behavior appears but remains inconsistent or support-dependent.
decision_rule.FAIL: Target behavior does not transfer despite sufficient evidence opportunity.
decision_rule.INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE: The task did not provide enough valid evidence to decide.

sessions.evidence: Friday result becomes new learner-state evidence; it does not automatically rewrite the learner state without the Jev decision and policy gates.

qa_blockers: activity has no traceable diagnosed/reported need
speaking performance receives correction before the performance ends
Friday transfer reuses the practised scenario
activity does not contribute to the weekly Can-Do
publishing changes the existing B2 course or learner records
